title: Postpartum Psychosis Is Rare, Severe, and Treatable
hook: A Boston-area murder trial has put a little-known illness in the spotlight — one psychiatrists say is too often missed until it becomes a crisis.
key_points: Postpartum psychosis is distinct from postpartum depression and far more severe.
It can involve delusions or hallucinations and is treated as a medical emergency.
Psychiatrists say diagnosis and treatment for it remain inadequate.
The illness became visible through a criminal trial rather than routine care.
New or worsening confusion, paranoia, or hallucinations after birth need urgent help.
content_html: A trial near Boston, in which a mother is accused of killing her children and her defense argues she had postpartum psychosis, has drawn attention to an illness most people have never heard of. Psychiatrists quoted by NPR hope the attention pushes toward better diagnosis and treatment.
extra_html:
Postpartum psychosis is not a severe version of postpartum depression — it is a different illness. It can involve delusions, hallucinations, and a break from reality, and it comes on fast, usually in the weeks after birth. Clinicians treat it as a psychiatric emergency, because the risk to both parent and baby is real and the condition responds to treatment when it's caught.

The uncomfortable part of this story is how the illness became visible: through a courtroom rather than through routine postpartum care. That is roughly the point the psychiatrists are making. The practical takeaway for anyone around a new parent is a low threshold for concern — confusion, paranoia, hearing things, or thoughts of harm are not "baby blues" and warrant urgent help the same day, not at the next scheduled visit.

related.title: Recognizing Depression and Anxiety
related.hook: Depression and anxiety are among the most common — and most treatable — health conditions. Knowing the signs is the first step to getting help that works.

related.title: What Mental Health Really Means
related.hook: Mental health isn't just the absence of illness — it's being able to cope with life's stresses, work, learn, and contribute. Everyone has it, and it can be cared for.

flashcards.prompt: How does postpartum psychosis differ from postpartum depression?

choices.text: It's far more severe and can involve delusions or hallucinations
It's a milder form that resolves on its own
It only affects mood, never perception or thinking

flashcards.explanation_html: Postpartum psychosis is a distinct and much more serious illness — it can involve a break from reality and is treated as a medical emergency.

flashcards.prompt: What should someone do if a new parent shows confusion, paranoia, or hallucinations after birth?
flashcards.back_html: Seek urgent medical help — this is treated as an emergency, not a wait-and-see symptom. Delay is the main danger.

flashcards.prompt: What gap did psychiatrists point to in this case?
flashcards.back_html: That diagnosis and treatment for postpartum psychosis remain inadequate — the illness often surfaces only in crisis rather than being caught in routine care.
